title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026 (week 45) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report is based on data up to week 44 of 2026 (26 October to 1 November 2026) [N5].
analysis.location_and_population: The report covers England, focusing on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) activity across various populations, including those aged 65 years and over, individuals in clinical risk groups, and those aged 2 and 3 years [N4].
analysis.event: The report summarizes surveillance data for influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in England, noting that influenza activity is above baseline levels, RSV activity is at baseline levels, and SARS-CoV-2 activity has decreased and is circulating at low levels [N4, N19, N24].
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Influenza ED attendances increased slightly and were above seasonally expected levels, while the number of influenza-confirmed ARI incidents decreased compared with the previous week. For SARS-CoV-2, ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness remained stable, and confirmed ARI incidents decreased. RSV ED attendances increased and were within seasonally expected levels [N7, N8, N20, N21, N25].
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report indicates that influenza activity is now above baseline levels, and a briefing note has been issued to inform the NHS. There are noted issues with data collection, including misclassification of pharmacy vaccinations and incomplete data in weeks 41 and 42, which have been corrected since week 43 [N9, N10, N11, N13, N14, N15].

analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 5 November 2026 (week 45) provides an overview of respiratory virus activity in England. It notes that influenza is circulating at low levels, with ED attendances for influenza-like illness slightly above seasonally expected levels. SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) activity has decreased, with confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents declining compared to the previous week. RSV activity increased and is at baseline levels. The report highlights data collection challenges, including misclassification of pharmacy vaccinations and incomplete data in weeks 41 and 42, which have been corrected since week 43. A briefing note was issued to inform the NHS about influenza activity exceeding baseline levels. The data is based on the Moving Epidemic Method (MEM) and Mean Standard Deviation (MSD) for defining activity thresholds, with the latter now used for influenza and SARS-CoV-2 laboratory surveillance. The unified sample dataset (USD) is used to calculate SARS-CoV-2 test positivity rates, which decreased slightly in week 44 to 7.6% compared to 8.1% the previous week. Positivity rates remained stable among those aged 85 years and over, at 11.1%.
analysis.summary_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 5 November 2026 (week 45) provides an overview of respiratory virus activity in England.
